page: Microsoft Azure FX12ms_v2 is a compute-focused, memory-intensive virtual machine engineered around Intel Xeon 8573C processors. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 12 vCPUs mapped across 6 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for hardware-accelerated integer matrix computations. There are no discrete GPUs allocated, and local disk storage is not included, requiring the use of remote premium storage volumes.

A primary architectural characteristic of the FX12ms_v2 is its extreme memory-to-core allocation, provisioning 252.0 GB of total RAM, or 21.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration enables massive caching capability alongside substantial raw memory throughput, measuring 94.15 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 59.4 GB/sec for uncached writes. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier single-core performance, delivering a Geekbench single-core score of 2349.0 and top-tier text processing at 3015.0 points. Single-threaded compression workflows also show marked strength, generating 34.88 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.47 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression.

Workloads executing integer-driven or low-parameter model inference benefit from the CPU architecture, achieving a top-tier 339.89 tokens/sec for text generation with small 135M language models. Multi-core performance metrics, such as a PassMark CPU score of 22837.22 and a multi-threaded Geekbench score of 11866.0, balance in the middle 50% tier, constrained by the 6 physical core count. Similarly, Redis throughput yields 18.98 million SET operations per second.

Because the server packages high per-core clock frequencies and a massive memory density relative to its 12 vCPUs, it delivers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require heavy per-thread processing and large memory capacity without incurring licensing or operational overhead for unused core counts. The lack of local NVMe storage represents a key tradeoff, necessitating remote storage design. The FX12ms_v2 is suited for in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), complex financial modeling, compute-bound analytics, and memory-bound batch processing.
description: Microsoft Azure FX12ms_v2 is a high-frequency, memory-intensive server driven by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the configuration pairs 12 vCPUs (6 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading) and a large 260 MB L3 cache with 252.0 GB of system memory, providing 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled GPUs and features no local disk storage, depending entirely on remote storage. The platform integrates AVX-512 and Intel AMX vector instructions, delivering top-tier Geekbench single-core performance of 2349.0 points, strong single-threaded gzip compression at 34.88 GB/sec, and high-throughput inference on compact language models. While its core count yields average multi-core results, the high memory density and elevated clock rates make the FX12ms_v2 suitable for memory-heavy in-memory databases, EDA pipelines, and cache-intensive analytics.
